review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.original_summary: gh-api-utils.ts in shared/ contains both low-level API utilities (GhApiClient, parseApiJson) and a high-level token resolution function (resolveGitHubToken) that understands GitHub App installation semantics

review::.::holistic::ai_generated_debt::.original_summary: Docstrings on type definitions restate the type name without adding insight

isPermanentError in retry-utils.ts uses a broad string-matching heuristic against error messages to decide if an error is retryable. The CORE_PERMANENT_ERROR_PATTERNS list is well-curated but pattern-matching against error strings is inherently fragile.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.original_summary: Two unrelated interfaces named 'FileChange' exist in different modules with different shapes, both re-exported from barrel files
Four closely related types represent file changes with overlapping but slightly different shapes, creating confusion about which to use where
runLifecycleCheck has 6 positional parameters — exceeds public API parameter threshold

review::.::holistic::authorization_consi.original_summary: Azure and GitLab PR strategies receive a `token` parameter in CloseExistingPROptions and PRStrategyOptions but never use it. The token field exists because the interface is shared with GitHub, but Azure/GitLab silently ignore it, relying on CLI-level auth (az/glab login). This is documented in the type comments but could confuse callers.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.original_summary: parseManifestContent docstring describes V2->V3 migration but code does V2->V3->V4 and V3->V4
resolveGitHubToken docstring misrepresents skipped=true semantics (includes GH_TOKEN condition that code ignores)
validateForSync @throws clause says 'files section is missing or empty' but it validates files OR settings

review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.original_summary: All three PR strategies (GitHub, Azure, GitLab) handle unknown merge modes by returning { success: false, message: 'Unknown merge mode' } instead of throwing. This is consistent across strategies but inconsistent with the broader pattern where invalid inputs throw ValidationError.
Three different names for identical plain-object check: isObject, isPlainObject, isObjectContent
LifecycleAction and LifecycleReportInput are structurally identical interfaces in the same file

review::.::holistic::cross_module_archit.original_summary: 3 sync/ files import FileAction from vcs/pr-creator.ts re-export instead of canonical vcs/types.ts
output/github-summary.ts reads process.env directly, violating the codebase's DI principle for non-CLI code
shared/index.ts barrel omits 7 of 15 modules, causing 134 direct cross-module imports
vcs/index.ts barrel omits critical interfaces (IGitOps, IPRStrategy, GitAuthOptions), forcing direct imports
sync/types.ts imports GitOpsOptions from concrete vcs/git-ops.ts instead of a types file

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::d.original_summary: LifecycleReportInput and LifecycleAction are structurally identical interfaces

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::v.original_summary: validateSettings takes 5 params where 3 optional ones form an existing but unused context object

review::.::holistic::error_consistency::.original_summary: closeExistingPR silently returns false for both 'no PR' and 'close failed', losing error context
CommitPushManager detects push rejections via message substring matching instead of typed errors
writeGitHubStepSummary does not handle appendFileSync errors, silently failing on I/O issues

review::.::holistic::incomplete_migratio.original_summary: shared/env.ts interpolateEnvVars reads process.env directly (line 56). While this is the module's core purpose (reading env vars for template interpolation), the CLAUDE.md architecture principle says shared modules should not access process.env. An env-reader function could be injected.

Logger.debug() reads process.env.DEBUG and process.env.XFG_DEBUG directly at call time instead of accepting a debug-enabled flag at construction. The codebase has otherwise completed migration away from process.env in shared modules, but Logger retains this direct coupling.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::redu.original_summary: Redundant truthiness check before numeric comparison in diffSummary

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::unre.original_summary: Unreachable 'Unknown merge mode' dead code in three PR strategy merge() methods

review::.::holistic::low_level_elegance:.original_summary: loadManifest and parseManifestContent duplicate the V1-V4 migration chain

normalizer.ts contains two nearly parallel merge pipelines: mergeSettings (for final normalized output) and mergeRawSettings (for group-layer accumulation). Both handle rulesets, labels, repo settings, and deleteOrphaned with similar logic but different type signatures. The structural overlap creates maintenance risk — changes to merge semantics must be made in both places.
runLifecyclePhase and runFileSyncPhase take 6-7 positional params despite RepoIterationContext

validateForSync and the early guard in validateRawConfig both check for the presence of files/settings/groups using nearly identical logic. hasActionableSettings is used in validateForSync but the parallel check in validateRawConfig uses inline logic with different structure (hasFiles, hasSettings, hasGroupFiles, hasGroupSettings).
validateRawConfig and validateForSync duplicate hasGroupFiles/hasGroupSettings boolean expressions

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.original_summary: Sync modules import FileAction from vcs/pr-creator.ts bypassing the barrel export at vcs/index.ts

pr-creator.ts exposes createPR() and mergePR() as free functions that internally construct a PRStrategy via getPRStrategy() and (for create) wrap it in PRWorkflowExecutor. Meanwhile, PRMergeHandler and BranchManager also call getPRStrategy() separately. This means PRStrategy instances are created multiple times per repo (once in BranchManager.setupBranch for closeExistingPR, once in createPR, once in mergePR), with no reuse.

GitHub token resolution happens in two places during sync: once in processSingleRepo (line 353-363) to get repoToken for lifecycle/settings, and again inside AuthOptionsBuilder.resolve() when the processor runs. When the caller passes the pre-resolved token, AuthOptionsBuilder short-circuits, but if it doesn't (or passes undefined), the resolution runs again. This creates a subtle data-flow dependency where callers must remember to pre-resolve.

shared/gh-api-utils.ts bundles infrastructure-level API utilities (GhApiClient, parseApiJson, isHttp404Error) with business-level token resolution (resolveGitHubToken with GitHub App installation awareness). These serve different abstraction levels and different consumers.
